about: Longer context for the sample rows, keyed by title (lower case). Used by MOCK mode and the landing-page example so expanded rows show what a real build writes.

details.dashboard on the new revenue data model: The replacement for the current billing dashboard, rebuilt on the new revenue data model so Finance closes the quarter from one set of numbers instead of reconciling two. Engineering estimates 6 to 8 weeks, which leaves little room before the Q3 close on Sept 30, an external reporting deadline that does not move. It depends on the billing to revenue pipeline being backfilled first. The export button is in scope, so the build has to include it. Done when Finance can close one month end to end in the new dashboard without falling back to the old one.
details.export button for finance reconciliation: The CSV export from the old dashboard, rebuilt in the new one. About half of Finance does its monthly reconciliation through this export, so without it they cannot close in the new tool. The VP of Finance confirmed it is in scope for Sept 30, which means Engineering builds it rather than the team documenting a workaround. The open question is which reports and columns it must reproduce; regional teams that reconcile in local currency first may need a different layout. Done when every regional team can produce its reconciliation file from the new dashboard.
details.billing to revenue model data pipeline: The pipeline that moves billing records into the new revenue data model, including the backfill of historical invoices so past periods line up. The notes flag historical invoices as the messy part, and Data engineering has warned the backfill could slip a week if the 2023 records need cleanup. Everything else depends on it: the dashboard cannot be validated until the numbers underneath are right. Done when all historical invoices are on the new model and a sample month matches the old figures.
details.export workaround guide for finance: A written fallback for Finance in case the export button slips past go-live. Originally the main plan, now insurance, since the export is in scope and Engineering is building it. It should cover how to pull the same data another way, who to ask when numbers look wrong, and how regional teams that reconcile in local currency should handle the conversion. Worth drafting even if it is never used, because Q3 close cannot wait for a late feature.
details.agent walkthrough for support: A thirty minute walkthrough for Support agents on what changes for them, recorded so later hires can watch it. The account lookup flow is different in the new dashboard, and the Support lead said either way is fine for their team without having looked at the agent impact. Support named a tier 2 lead as the owner for agent training, who wants the session recorded. It should be booked before go-live so agents are not learning it from customer tickets.
details.go-live faq for regional finance leads: A short guide for the regional finance leads, especially outside the US, who run a different close calendar and some of whom reconcile in local currency first. It should answer what changes in their workflow, when the switch happens relative to their close, where the export lives, and who to contact. The EMEA and APAC leads asked for their own walkthrough, so this FAQ backs that up in writing. Done when every regional lead has it before their first close on the new dashboard.
details.weekly reconciliation check report: A weekly report showing how many reconciliations Finance completed in the new tool versus the old one, so the team can see adoption as it happens rather than after close. It is waiting on a definition of done from Finance: what counts as a completed reconciliation is not yet agreed. Once that is settled, the report needs an owner to run and share it each week.
details.scope and date briefing for the vp of fi: A one to one with the VP of Finance to lock Sept 30 as the go-live date and confirm the export button is in scope. The VP has escalated twice and Q3 close depends on this work, so they are the strongest champion, but scope decisions need to be on record before Engineering commits. The outcome to capture: the date in writing, the export in or out, and what drops first if the build slips.
details.agent walkthrough of the changes: The session where Support agents see the new account lookup flow and the other changes that affect them. Booked for week 4. The Support lead owns getting agents into the room; the tier 2 lead runs it and wants it recorded for later hires. It should come early enough that agents can try the new flow before customers start asking about it.
details.workflow demo for regional finance leads: A demo call with the regional finance leads to show what changes for their workflow and gather objections before the build locks. Held on the 12th. The non-US leads use the dashboard differently, run a different close calendar, and some reconcile in local currency first, so their feedback can change what the export has to produce. Follow-ups from the call should feed the export requirements and the go-live FAQ.
details.go-live announcement to finance and supp: The announcement that tells Finance and Support the go-live date, when training happens, and what breaks and when. Goes by email and at the all hands. It needs an owner; right now nobody is named. It should land after training dates are fixed and before the last close on the old dashboard, so nobody is surprised mid-close.
details.feedback session after the first close: A session after the first quarter close on the new dashboard to hear what worked and what did not, run with Finance ops. It is the first real test of the export and the regional workflows, so it should capture problems while they are fresh and decide which fixes are needed before the next close.
details.weekly migration update email: A short weekly email to everyone affected: what shipped, what is next, and any dates that moved. It keeps Finance, Support and the regional leads from finding out about changes late. It is waiting on someone to own progress reporting, since nobody has been named to gather the updates each week.
details.support owner named and confirmed: Tracks whether Support has put a named person, not just the team, on the hook for agent readiness. Without one, training cannot be scheduled and the account lookup changes reach agents through customer tickets. The tier 2 lead is the likely owner; this is met when that is confirmed in writing.
details.regional finance leads walked through: Tracks how many regional finance leads have seen what changes for them. The non-US leads matter most, since they run a different close calendar and some reconcile in local currency first. Met when every lead has had the walkthrough before their first close on the new dashboard.
details.export workaround documented and signed: Tracks whether the fallback for the export button is written down and approved by Finance, in case the export slips past go-live. It is insurance: the export is in scope, but Q3 close cannot wait for a late feature.
details.finance reconciliations completed in new: The main outcome: the share of monthly reconciliations Finance completes in the new dashboard rather than the old one. The aim is all of them by the first close after go-live. A shortfall usually means the export does not yet produce what some team needs, often a regional team working in local currency.
details.reconciliations completed in the new too: The main outcome: the share of monthly reconciliations Finance completes in the new dashboard rather than the old one. The aim is all of them by the first close after go-live. A shortfall usually means the export does not yet produce what some team needs, often a regional team working in local currency.
details.support tickets about the dashboard: Counts Support tickets about the new dashboard each week after go-live. The aim is under 10 a week by week 2. A high count means agent training did not land or the account lookup change is confusing customers, and should prompt a second walkthrough.
details.hours of manual reconciliation per week: Measures how much manual work Finance still does each week to reconcile the numbers. The point of the migration is one set of numbers, so this should fall from the current baseline by Q4. If it does not drop, the migration has not delivered what it was for, however smoothly it launched.
